# Grzybodex app privacy policy

**Version:** 5 · **Effective from:** 2026-11-20

This is a translation; the Polish version prevails.

## 1. Key points in brief

- **Grzybodex works on your phone.** There are no accounts, no sign-in and no server of our own.
- **Mushroom photos are recognised on the phone**, by a model stored in the app. We do not send them automatically. Only if you yourself report a mushroom from your collection to the atlas can you e-mail the creator up to 3 photos — see section 5.
- The collection, saved spots, the trail and the settings stay in the phone's storage.
- The app has no ads, no analytics and no crash reporting. We do not sell data and we do not build profiles.
- The app connects to the internet only to download the **map background** (OpenTopoMap tiles in the “Detailed” view) or an **offline voivodeship map** when you download it yourself — see section 5. The browser opens only when you tap a link to an external website.

## 2. Who is behind the app

The app is made by: **[CREATOR CONTACT DETAILS — TO BE COMPLETED: full name or business name and e-mail address]**.

Data saved in the app stays on your phone. The creator does not receive a copy and has no access to it, unless you yourself send a mushroom report (section 5). You can send questions about privacy to the address above.

## 3. What data the app stores

Everything below stays only in your phone's storage.

| What | When it is created | Where and for how long |
|---|---|---|
| **Photos for recognition** (up to 3 shots of one mushroom, from the camera or the gallery) | when you take or choose a photo in the scanner | for the duration of the scan, in memory and in the app's temporary files; the system may delete them later |
| **Collection entry:** date, recognised species, probability, number of shots, warnings and a copy of the first photo | only when you save the result yourself | in the app's database and folder, until you clear the app's data or uninstall it |
| **My spots:** name, note, coordinates, date and the location of the parked car | only when you save a spot yourself | in the app's database, until you delete the spot, clear the app's data or uninstall it |
| **Settings:** app language, text size and bold text, colours, selected regions, confirmation of the safety rules (with the date), which badges have already been shown | when you change something or confirm the rules | in the app's settings storage, until you clear the app's data or uninstall it |
| **Trail:** GPS location points (coordinates, accuracy, time) about every 10 m | only after you tap “Record trail” on the Map tab, until you tap “Stop” — also with the screen off | in the app's database, until “Delete trail”, recording a new trail (it replaces the previous one), clearing the app's data or uninstalling it |
| **Current phone location and step count** | when you have the map or the guidance to a spot open and you allow location (steps: when you allow physical activity) | only in the memory of the running app; they are not saved unless you save a spot yourself |

The photo in the collection is an unchanged copy of the original. If the original contained data added by the camera (e.g. where and when it was taken), the copy contains it too. It stays on the phone.

When you report a mushroom (section 5), the app creates up to 3 downsized copies of the photos as JPEG files without EXIF metadata, and a zgloszenie.json file. They stay in the app's cache. The system may delete them.

The app does not store your name, e-mail address, phone number or advertising ID. It does not record sound.

## 4. App permissions on the phone

- **Camera** — to take photos of a mushroom in the scanner. We ask for permission at the first scan. Without permission you can choose a photo from the gallery.
- **Photos (gallery)** — when you want to recognise a mushroom from an existing photo. The app reads only the photos you select.
- **Location** — permission “while using the app”. It is used to show your position on the map sketch, to save a spot, and for the distance and direction to saved spots (also using the compass). Without permission the app shows a clearly marked demo point (Gdańsk, Lasy Oliwskie) and does not know your location.
- **Location while recording a trail** — when you turn on “Record trail” yourself, the app reads the location also with the screen off or in the background. During all that time the phone shows the notification “Grzybodex is recording your trail”. Recording ends when you tap “Stop”. The app does not ask for “always” location permission.
- **Notifications** — only to show the trail-recording notification. Without this permission the trail is recorded the same way, but the notification may be hidden.
- **Physical activity (step counter)** — when GPS loses the signal while you walk, the app estimates your position from the step count and the compass and clearly marks it as estimated. We ask for permission on the screen that guides you to a spot. Steps are not saved. Without permission the app uses GPS only.

You can withdraw permission at any time in the phone settings: **Settings → Apps → Grzybodex → Permissions** (menu names depend on the phone manufacturer).

## 5. Internet and recipients of data

- **The app sends nothing by itself.** Photos, saved spots, the trail, steps, the collection and the settings do not leave the phone. The exception is a mushroom report that you yourself send by e-mail (the next two points). The app has no server of its own and no accounts, and it does not use analytics, advertising or error-reporting services.
- **Mushroom report (only if you send it yourself).** You start a report in the Collection tab, at a saved scan (“Report to the atlas”); it is not on the result screen. Before your mail app opens, the app shows what will happen. The form has: photos from the saved scan (up to 3), a name (optional), a description (up to 1000 characters), a habitat from a list, the date found (by default the scan date), the voivodeship (optional; never exact coordinates), a choice of licence for the photos and description, and two required declarations: that the photos are yours and your consent to processing. Then the app opens your e-mail app with a ready e-mail to the creator. The e-mail contains: a subject, text with the form fields, the app version, up to 3 photos and a zgloszenie.json file with the same data (and with the species identifier from your collection, if there is one). The photos are downsized and saved again as JPEG without EXIF metadata (no GPS, phone model or date). We do not attach location, coordinates or model results. You see the whole e-mail and decide yourself whether to send it. The e-mail goes through your e-mail provider (e.g. Gmail), under its privacy policy. The creator therefore also receives your e-mail address and anything you write yourself. Do not enter data you do not want to disclose.
- **What the creator does with a report.** The creator checks it by hand. A report does not change the edibility category of any species. The creator uses it only to check the mushroom and possibly add a species to the catalogue. The creator does not use reports to train the recognition model without your separate consent. In the report you choose the licence under which the creator may publish the photos and description: CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0 — or “for the creator’s eyes only”, i.e. no publication. Creative Commons licences are irrevocable: once granted, you cannot take it back. Withdrawing consent to the processing of data does not withdraw the licence for photos and descriptions that have already been published. The legal basis for processing is your consent: you send the e-mail of your own free will (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Providing the data is voluntary. You can withdraw consent at any time by writing to the address in section 2. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of what was done before. The creator keeps the report until the species is added or a decision not to add it, and no longer than 12 months. Then the creator deletes it. The creator receives reports through the creator’s own e-mail provider.
- **The map background comes from OpenTopoMap** (tile.opentopomap.org, data © OpenStreetMap, CC-BY-SA licence). When you view the Map tab with the internet on, the phone downloads from this server the tiles of the area visible on the screen. The server therefore sees the phone's IP address and the area you are viewing, i.e. approximately where you are. We do not send it coordinates, spots, the trail or any user identifier. Downloaded tiles stay in the phone's cache. The “Overview” view uses only the map of Poland built into the app and does not connect to the internet. Without the internet the map shows the built-in map of Poland and the downloaded voivodeship maps.
- **Offline maps.** When you tap “Download” yourself on the “Offline maps” screen, the phone downloads the map file of the chosen voivodeship from the map-pack server. That server sees the phone's IP address and which file you download (i.e. the chosen voivodeship and level of detail). We do not send it coordinates, spots, the trail or any user identifier. Downloaded maps stay in the phone's storage until you delete them.
- **Links to external websites** (e.g. gov.pl, Creative Commons licences, source pages) open in the phone's browser only after you tap them. The website then sees, among other things, your IP address and works under its own privacy policy. Tapping the emergency number 112 opens the phone app.
- **Android backup.** The app allows the Android system to include its data in backups. If you have backup turned on in your phone, the system may save the app's data (including the collection, spots and the trail) in your Google account, under Google's terms. You can turn this off or delete the backup in the phone and Google account settings.

## 6. How to delete your data

- **Spot:** on the Map tab, expand the spot and choose “Delete”. A new “car” spot replaces the previous one.
- **Trail:** on the Map tab, choose “Delete trail”. A new trail replaces the previous one.
- **Settings:** you can change them in the app's Settings.
- **Offline maps:** delete them with “Delete” on the Settings → Offline maps screen.
- **Collection:** the app has no button for deleting single entries. You delete the entries and the saved photos together with the rest of the app's data.
- **Mushroom report:** write to the address in section 2 and give the address the report came from. The creator will delete the report and the photos (except photos and descriptions already published under a Creative Commons licence). You delete your own copy of the e-mail in your e-mail app. Temporary files in the app disappear when you clear the app's data or when the system deletes them.
- **Everything at once:** on the phone choose **Settings → Apps → Grzybodex → Storage → Clear data** or uninstall the app. You delete the backup in your Google account separately, as described above.

## 7. Your rights

The creator does not receive your data from the app, so you exercise the rights given by the GDPR ([Regulation (EU) 2016/679](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)) mainly yourself, on your phone (exception: a mushroom report, the last point below):

- **access** — you can see the saved data in the app,
- **erasure** — as in section 6,
- **objection and restriction** — you can refuse permission for the camera, gallery, location and physical activity, or not save results, spots and the trail,
- **mushroom report** — if you send one, the creator is the controller of the data in that e-mail. You can write to the address in section 2 to ask for access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing or withdrawal of consent.

If you believe that someone is processing your personal data unlawfully, you can lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych, [uodo.gov.pl](https://uodo.gov.pl)).

## 8. Data security on the phone

The app's data is kept in its own folder, which other apps usually cannot access. The app does not encrypt it separately. It is protected by the Android system and your phone's screen lock.

## 9. Changes to the policy

The current version is always in the app: **Settings → Privacy policy**. We mark changes with a new version number and the date at the top of the document.
